questions.prompt: What is the intent of the Adapter pattern?

options.text: Convert the interface of a class into another interface clients expect
Add new behavior to an object while keeping its interface
Provide a simplified interface to a complex subsystem

questions.explanation: Adapter changes one interface into a different expected one. Adding behavior = Decorator; simplifying a subsystem = Facade; controlling access = Proxy.

questions.prompt: Match each Adapter participant to its role.

pairs.right: The interface the client wants to use
The existing class with an incompatible interface
Implements the target and delegates to the adaptee

questions.explanation: The adapter implements the Target and forwards calls to the Adaptee, so the Client only sees the Target.

questions.prompt: Why do TypeScript adapters typically use composition (an 'object adapter')?

options.text: The adapter holds the adaptee, which suits TypeScript's single-inheritance classes
Because TypeScript supports multiple inheritance of classes

questions.explanation: Class adapters need multiple inheritance; TypeScript classes have single inheritance, so the adapter composes (holds) the adaptee.

questions.prompt: Adapter is most useful at integration ____ — third-party libraries or legacy modules whose interface you can't change.
questions.explanation: Adapters belong at boundaries you don't own or shouldn't modify, centralizing the translation there.

questions.prompt: How does Adapter differ from Facade?

options.text: Adapter makes one interface look like a different expected interface; Facade simplifies a complex subsystem
Adapter adds behavior; Facade removes behavior
Adapter controls access; Facade clones objects

questions.explanation: Adapter is about interface conversion; Facade is about presenting a simpler front to many classes.

questions.prompt: Which is a sign you might be MISUSING Adapter?

options.text: Using it to hide a mismatch between two interfaces you own and could align directly
Using it to wrap a third-party library you can't modify
Keeping the adapter thin and free of business logic
Letting the client depend only on the Target interface

questions.explanation: Adapters are for boundaries you can't change; adapting code you own can just paper over an inconsistent design you should fix.
